source_refs.note: PDF 220 (book p. 218): 7.1.1 Scalars, definition and the examples distance and speed

blocks.text: Pyare bachon, motion ki baat karne se pehle humein quantities (miqdaar) ki do qismein samajhni hain: scalars aur vectors. Yeh farq is poore unit ki buniyaad hai, kyun ke aage har sawal mein aap ko yeh dhyan rakhna hoga ke koi cheez sirf "kitni" hai, ya "kitni aur kis taraf". Is sabaq mein pehli qism: scalars.
Kitab ki definition: scalar quantities woh hain jo sirf magnitude (size ya numerical value, yani kitni hai) se poori tarah bayan ho jati hain. Scalars ki koi direction (simt) nahin hoti.

items: Distance: safar kiye gaye raaste ki kul lambai, direction ki parwah kiye baghair.
Speed: woh rate (raftaar) jis se fi unit time distance tay hota hai, direction ki parwah kiye baghair.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
"Magnitude" ka matlab hai number apni unit ke saath, jaise 5 km ya 20 m/s. Scalar ke liye bas yehi poori baat hai. Aap 5 km chale, chahe mashriq (east) ki taraf ya maghrib (west) ki taraf, chahe ghoom phir kar: distance 5 km hi rahega.
Distance mein raaste ka har tukra jama hota hai. Is liye waqt guzarne ke saath distance ya to barhta hai ya wahi rehta hai (jab aap ruke hon), kabhi kam nahin hota, aur kabhi negative nahin hota.
Speed = distance fi unit time, yani \(\text{speed} = \frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}\). Iski aam units m/s aur km/h hain. Kyun ke
\[1\ \text{km/h} = \dfrac{1000\ \text{m}}{3600\ \text{s}}\]
\[= \dfrac{5}{18}\ \text{m/s},\]
is liye km/h ko m/s mein badalne ke liye \(\frac{5}{18}\) se multiply karein (misaal: \(36\) km/h \(= 36 \times \frac{5}{18} = 10\) m/s), aur wapas km/h banane ke liye \(\frac{18}{5}\) se. Yeh conversion exercise mein baar baar kaam aayegi, is liye abhi se yaad kar lijiye.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh hamari misaal hai, kitab ki nahin.) Ali ghar se 3 km bazaar gaya aur phir 3 km wapas ghar aa gaya; poore safar mein 1 ghanta laga. Us ka distance kitna hai aur average speed kitni?
Distance: raaste ke dono tukre jama karein: \(3 + 3 = 6\) km. Direction ki parwah nahin, kyun ke distance scalar hai.
Speed: \(\frac{6}{1} = 6\) km/h. m/s mein: \(6 \times \frac{5}{18} = \frac{5}{3} \approx 1.67\) m/s.
Dekhiye, Ali wapas wahin aa gaya jahan se chala tha, phir bhi distance zero nahin. Yehi baat agle sabaq mein displacement se farq banayegi.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Kya speedometer (gaari ki speed wali sui) kabhi negative number dikhata hai, jab gaari reverse mein chal rahi ho tab bhi? Nahin! Speedometer speed dikhata hai, aur speed scalar hai, is liye hamesha zero ya positive.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Scalar ki sirf magnitude hoti hai (number + unit), direction nahin.
2. Distance = tay kiye gaye raaste ki kul lambai; kabhi negative nahin.
3. Speed = fi unit time tay kiya gaya distance; kabhi negative nahin.
4. \(1\) km/h \(= \frac{5}{18}\) m/s.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Distance ya speed ko negative likh dena. Yeh dono kabhi negative nahin hote; minus sign sirf vector quantities (displacement, velocity) ke saath aata hai, jo agle sabaq (7.1.2) mein hain.
2. Units mila dena, jaise kilometre ko second se divide kar dena, ya minutes aur hours ko baghair convert kiye jama kar dena. Pehle sab units ek jaisi karein, phir hisaab karein.
